analysis: The only changed content in docs/reference/configuration.md falls in the ranges 969, 977-978, 1115 and 1712-1713. In this batch I could see line 969 (resource_policy_sha256 now documents the Qwen3.8-27B resident-assistant fields), lines 977-978 (evidence_sha256 and qualified_at for the assistant qualification) and line 1115 (the tensorAssistant validation note). Lines 1712-1713 are outside the supplied units, so they are unreviewed. This is a documentation-only change with no code, so no runtime control changes. Nothing in the visible lines touches the T-041 SSD cache storage posture: cache.daily_write_gb, cache.directory, the HMAC names, the TTL or the KEK handling. The assistant-related text describes cluster pair approval digests, which the coordinator (platform-owned) consumes, plus the claim that a tensorAssistant beside nativeMember is refused unless it is exactly the build-declared public assistant. That claim cannot be verified from this batch because the implementing source (ClusterConfiguration.validate, ClusterPublicTensorAssistant.resourcePolicyFields, ClusterPublicModels.tensorAssistant) was not supplied. The text widens the public-traffic cluster claims: it says the parity qualification is applied to the whole mode family on any Apple silicon pair, and that several pipelines rest on owner decisions without hardware records. That is documented residual risk, not a new regression, and the surrounding threat model (T-054, T-055, T-056) concerns the coordinator's overclaiming of qualification. The next pass should confirm that the code backing the new resource-policy digest composition matches the documentation, and that the evidence report docs/reports/2026-11-05-qwen27-public-assistant.md exists. No finding qualifies on the visible evidence.
